f3_program: collection("citrus_grove.orchards", "orchard", "citrus_grove", source("their sixteen orchards"))
observe(at("citrus_grove.orchards.count", "planned"), 16, "count", source("their sixteen orchards"))
observe(at("citrus_grove.orchards.lemons.count", "planned"), 8, "count", source("Lemons, their most popular citrus fruit, will take up eight orchards"))

fraction_of(at("citrus_grove.orchards.oranges.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.lemons.count", "planned"), 1, 2, source("Oranges are their second most popular fruit and will occupy half as many orchards as the lemons"))

sum_relation(at("citrus_grove.orchards.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.lemons.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.oranges.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.limes.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.grapefruits.count", "planned"), source("Lemons, their most popular citrus fruit, will take up eight orchards. Oranges are their second most popular fruit and will occupy half as many orchards as the lemons. Limes and grapefruits will split the remaining orchards."))
same(at("citrus_grove.orchards.limes.count", "planned"), at("citrus_grove.orchards.grapefruits.count", "planned"), source("Limes and grapefruits will split the remaining orchards"))
query("value", at("citrus_grove.orchards.grapefruits.count", "planned"))
assumptions: Interpreted "split the remaining orchards" as an even split between limes and grapefruits.

f3_program: collection("family.oranges", "orange", "family", source("their oranges"))
observe(at("family.car.passengers.count", "arrival"), 4, "count", source("A family of 4 arrives"))
observe(at("florida.promotion.orange_rate", "arrival"), 1, "orange_per_passenger", source("one orange per passenger"))

rate_relation(at("family.oranges.received.count", "arrival"), at("florida.promotion.orange_rate", "arrival"), at("family.car.passengers.count", "arrival"), source("every car that arrives gets one orange per passenger"))
add("promotion_oranges", "family", at("family.oranges.count", "current"), at("family.oranges.received.count", "arrival"), source("A family of 4 arrives and gets their oranges"))
observe(at("family.stop.planned_spending.amount", "planned"), 15, "dollar", source("they would spend $15 in total"))
observe(at("stop.orange.unit_price", "stop"), 1.5, "dollar_per_orange", source("the oranges would've cost $1.5 each"))

rate_relation(at("family.stop.oranges.would_be_cost.amount", "stop"), at("stop.orange.unit_price", "stop"), at("family.oranges.received.count", "arrival"), source("the oranges would've cost $1.5 each"))
same(at("family.money_saved.amount", "stop"), at("family.stop.oranges.would_be_cost.amount", "stop"), source("now that they have the oranges they don't have to buy them at the stop"))
query("percentage_ratio", at("family.money_saved.amount", "stop"), at("family.stop.planned_spending.amount", "planned"))
assumptions: The oranges whose purchase is avoided are the same oranges the family received through the promotion.

f3_program: collection("graveyard.skeletons", "skeleton", "graveyard", source("In a graveyard, there are 20 skeletons"))
observe(at("graveyard.skeletons.count", "current"), 20, "count", source("there are 20 skeletons"))
member("graveyard.skeletons", "graveyard.skeletons.adult_women", source("Half of these skeletons are adult women"))
member("graveyard.skeletons", "graveyard.skeletons.adult_men", source("the remaining number are split evenly between adult men and children"))
member("graveyard.skeletons", "graveyard.skeletons.children", source("the remaining number are split evenly between adult men and children"))
fraction_of(at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_women.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("Half of these skeletons are adult women"))

sum_relation(at("graveyard.skeletons.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_women.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_men.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.children.count", "current"), source("Half of these skeletons are adult women, and the remaining number are split evenly between adult men and children"))
same(at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_men.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.children.count", "current"), source("the remaining number are split evenly between adult men and children"))
observe(at("adult_woman.body.bones.count", "current"), 20, "count", source("an adult woman has 20 bones in their body"))
offset(at("adult_man.body.bones.count", "current"), at("adult_woman.body.bones.count", "current"), 5, "count", source("a male has 5 more than this"))
fraction_of(at("child.body.bones.count", "current"), at("adult_woman.body.bones.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("a child has half as many as an adult woman"))

product_relation(at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_women.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_women.count", "current"), at("adult_woman.body.bones.count", "current"), source("an adult woman has 20 bones in their body"))

product_relation(at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_men.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_men.count", "current"), at("adult_man.body.bones.count", "current"), source("a male has 5 more than this"))

product_relation(at("graveyard.skeletons.children.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.children.count", "current"), at("child.body.bones.count", "current"), source("a child has half as many as an adult woman"))

sum_relation(at("graveyard.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_women.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.adult_men.bones.count", "current"), at("graveyard.skeletons.children.bones.count", "current"), source("In a graveyard, there are 20 skeletons.  Half of these skeletons are adult women, and the remaining number are split evenly between adult men and children.  If an adult woman has 20 bones in their body, and a male has 5 more than this, and a child has half as many as an adult woman"))
query("value", at("graveyard.bones.count", "current"))
assumptions: Treated "a male" as an adult man from the preceding partition and each body-bone count as applying to every skeleton in that group.
The requested weekly quantity requires the unstated number of days in a week; F3-v1 forbids supplying that external time-unit ontology fact.

f3_program: observe(at("brendan.waiter.wage_rate", "this_week"), 6, "dollar_per_hour", source("Brendan makes $6/hour as a waiter"))
collection("brendan.schedule.shifts", "shift", "brendan.schedule", source("He's scheduled for 2 8-hour shifts and 1 12-hour shift this week"))
observe(at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shifts.count", "this_week"), 2, "count", source("2 8-hour shifts"))
observe(at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shift.duration", "this_week"), 8, "hour", source("8-hour shifts"))
observe(at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shifts.count", "this_week"), 1, "count", source("1 12-hour shift"))
observe(at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shift.duration", "this_week"), 12, "hour", source("12-hour shift"))

product_relation(at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shifts.hours.total", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shifts.count", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shift.duration", "this_week"), source("2 8-hour shifts"))

product_relation(at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shifts.hours.total", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shifts.count", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shift.duration", "this_week"), source("1 12-hour shift"))

sum_relation(at("brendan.work.hours.total", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.eight_hour_shifts.hours.total", "this_week"), at("brendan.schedule.twelve_hour_shifts.hours.total", "this_week"), source("He's scheduled for 2 8-hour shifts and 1 12-hour shift this week"))
rate_relation(at("brendan.wages.earned.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.waiter.wage_rate", "this_week"), at("brendan.work.hours.total", "this_week"), source("Brendan makes $6/hour as a waiter"))
observe(at("brendan.tips.mean_rate", "this_week"), 12, "dollar_per_hour", source("an average of $12 in tips each hour"))

rate_relation(at("brendan.tips.earned.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.tips.mean_rate", "this_week"), at("brendan.work.hours.total", "this_week"), source("He also makes an average of $12 in tips each hour"))
fraction_of(at("brendan.tips.reported.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.tips.earned.amount", "this_week"), 1, 3, source("he only reports 1/3rd of his tips to the IRS"))

sum_relation(at("brendan.income.reported.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.wages.earned.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.tips.reported.amount", "this_week"), source("Brendan is supposed to pay 20% of his income in taxes, but he only reports 1/3rd of his tips to the IRS"))

percent_of(at("brendan.taxes.paid.amount", "this_week"), at("brendan.income.reported.amount", "this_week"), 20, source("Brendan is supposed to pay 20% of his income in taxes, but he only reports 1/3rd of his tips to the IRS"))
query("value", at("brendan.taxes.paid.amount", "this_week"))
assumptions: Interpreted the partial tip reporting as leaving wage income fully reported, and the tax payment as applying to reported income.
